builder_plan.scenario: Long customer conversations exhaust memory or limit concurrent requests.
builder_plan.change: Change only the attention cache policy, after checking model and runtime support.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model with its ordinary attention cache.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak cache memory, long-context answer quality, first-token latency, and requests completed.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FlatCake: A Flat KVCache Storage Architecture for LLM Serving
summary: Replaces tiered DRAM-cache-over-SSD KV management (as in Mooncake) with a flat architecture that places each KV block once, in session-contiguous layer-major order, and streams SSD reads directly to GPU via GPUDirect Storage. Cost is a redesign of the serving storage path, dependence on NVMe SSDs with GPUDirect support, and commitment to a fixed placement decision at block creation time. It can fail when the deployment lacks GPUDirect-capable storage or multi-SSD bandwidth, when workloads are DRAM-resident and tiering is not the bottleneck, and when the trace-specific gains do not transfer to different session reuse patterns.
rationale: The gains are demonstrated on multi-tier, multi-GPU serving infrastructure with GPUDirect Storage that a single 24 GB GPU deployment cannot replicate, so the reader should track the approach rather than adopt it.
technique: Flat session-contiguous KV cache storage with GPUDirect

claims.statement: Replaces tiered DRAM-cache-over-SSD KV management (as in Mooncake) with a flat architecture that places each KV block once, in session-contiguous layer-major order, and streams SSD reads directly to GPU via GPUDirect Storage. Cost is a redesign of the serving storage path, dependence on NVMe SSDs with GPUDirect support, and commitment to a fixed placement decision at block creation time. It can fail when the deployment lacks GPUDirect-capable storage or multi-SSD bandwidth, when workloads are DRAM-resident and tiering is not the bottleneck, and when the trace-specific gains do not transfer to different session reuse patterns.

On a production Claude Code trace with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, FlatCake sustains a 94% cache hit rate versus 64% for Mooncake, eliminates 6.5x-6.7x SSD read amplification, and reduces peak-load mean TTFT by 1.6x while improving total token throughput by 1.6x; on Llama-3.1-70B it reduces mean TTFT by up to 2.4x over Mooncake and 1.8x over Mooncake-GDS.
